title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 104: The Terracotta Army: Ancient Guardians in Clay
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE — A2 (BAND 4.0) • TEST 104

The Terracotta Army: Ancient Guardians in Clay

Paragraph 1. In March 1974, the weather in northern China was very dry. A group of farmers near Xi'an decided to dig a well to find water. Several metres under the ground, their tools hit hard baked clay. Soon, they found broken pots, metal arrows, and a life-sized clay head. Local leaders called museum experts to check the field. This simple farm job led to a huge discovery: the Terracotta Army of Qin Shi Huang.

Paragraph 2. Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor of united China in 221 BCE. Shortly after he became ruler as a teenager, he ordered workers to build a giant underground city for his afterlife. A later Chinese history book says more than 700,000 workers spent almost forty years building it. Inside the tomb area, thousands of clay soldiers, horses, and wooden carts stood ready in neat army lines.

Paragraph 3. Workers used local clay to make the basic body parts, such as legs and arms, from reusable moulds. Then, skilled artists shaped each soldier's hair, ears, and face by hand. Because of this handwork, every single statue looked different. Master workers also pressed their own names onto hidden parts of each statue so bosses could check the quality.

Paragraph 4. Today, the clay soldiers look brown or grey. However, when they were first made, every warrior had bright red, green, blue, and purple paint over a natural tree layer. Sadly, when modern experts opened the ground, the dry air made the old paint fall off in minutes. Interestingly, the bronze swords found with the soldiers were still clean and sharp after two thousand years because the surrounding earth protected them.

groups.title: Questions 5–7
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

steps: Đoạn 1: "farmers near Xi'an decided to dig a well to find water." → Từ cần điền: well.
Đoạn 2: "Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor of united China..." → Từ cần điền: emperor.
Đoạn 3: "make the basic body parts... from reusable moulds." → Từ cần điền: moulds.
Đoạn 3: "pressed their own names onto hidden parts of each statue..." → Từ cần điền: names.

q5.text: Why did museum experts visit the farmers' field in 1974?
options: A. They wanted to help farmers find water during dry weather.
B. Farmers uncovered ancient clay statues and weapons in the soil.
C. The Chinese government planned to build a new road there.
D. An old history book showed the exact map of the tomb.

steps: Đoạn 1: Nông dân đào thấy mảnh gốm, mũi tên đồng và đầu tượng đất nung rồi báo cho chính quyền gọi chuyên gia → Chọn B.

q6.text: When did Qin Shi Huang order workers to start building his tomb?
options: A. While he was still a teenager.
B. Forty years after he united China.
C. Shortly before he died as an old man.
D. When local farmers discovered the clay heads.

steps: Đoạn 2: "Shortly after he became ruler as a teenager, he ordered workers to build..." → Chọn A.

q7.text: What surprised experts about the bronze swords found with the soldiers?
options: A. They were painted in bright purple and green colours.
B. They fell apart as soon as dry air touched them.
C. They stayed clean and sharp for two thousand years.
D. They were made out of baked clay instead of metal.

steps: Đoạn 4: "the bronze swords found with the soldiers were still clean and sharp after two thousand years..." → Chọn C.
